mainTopic: How to place the two back burial niches (כוכין) in a burial cave without disrespect or overlap, and the start of a new discussion on finding buried bodies.
overview: The משנה teaches that a burial cave has eight כוכין: three on each side wall and two on the wall opposite the entrance. The גמרא rejects one way of placing the back two niches, calling it 'a burial of donkeys' because it is disrespectful. According to רבי יוחנן, the two niches are dug diagonally out of the back corners. The גמרא objects that these corner niches would run into the niches next to them. רב אשי answers that they are dug lower in the wall, and he proves this from רבי שמעון's four caves around a courtyard, which could not be built any other way. רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע suggests the four caves could instead work by slanting the niches like palm leaves, but the גמרא shows with a measurement of the diagonal that eight niches cannot fit, so his idea is a mistake. A second answer to the corner problem is that those niches were small ones for נפלים. Finally, the גמרא opens a new topic by quoting a משנה in נזיר about finding one or two bodies buried in the normal way.

steps.title: That arrangement is disrespectful
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects a proposed way of arranging the niches, because it would be like burying donkeys.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is a burial of donkeys!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects a way of arranging the niches that was just suggested. It says this setup would treat the dead without proper respect.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem with this suggestion is not space. The problem is dignity. The גמרא says this arrangement treats the dead the way donkeys are buried, so it needs a different, respectful arrangement.

keyTerms.meaning: Burial of donkeys: a disrespectful, careless way of burying
Burial niches dug into the walls of a cave

phrases.english: This is a burial of donkeys!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the arrangement suggested just before this point in the daf.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proposed arrangement of the two niches opposite the entrance.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It is undignified for the dead, like a burial of donkeys.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: place them in the corners
steps.stepSummary: According to רבי יוחנן, the two back niches are dug diagonally out of the two back corners.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to רבי יוחנן, he makes them in the corner.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new, respectful arrangement based on רבי יוחנן. The two niches go in the back corners of the cave, pointing out at an angle.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Putting the niches diagonally in the corners avoids the disrespectful arrangement that was just rejected. This solves the dignity problem from step 1, and the next step checks whether it causes a space problem.

keyTerms.meaning: A corner, where two walls meet
He makes them, meaning he digs the niches

phrases.english: According to Rabbi Yoḥanan,
he makes them in the corner.
phrases.notes: Each of the two niches goes in its own back corner, pointing out diagonally.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן, דְּעָבֵיד לְהוּ בְּקֶרֶן זָוִית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a respectful arrangement after the previous one was rejected.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: There seemed to be no respectful place for the two niches.
steps.terutzMaskana: They are dug diagonally out of the corners.

steps.title: The corner niches would touch
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that niches in the corner would run into the neighboring niches.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the niches touch one another!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יוחנן's corner plan. If you dig a diagonal niche in the corner, it will crash into the niches next to it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each back corner already has a niche going into the side wall and one going into the back wall. A third, diagonal niche between them would overlap with their inner ends. Then none of them would have enough room.

keyTerms.meaning: They touch, run into each other
One another

phrases.english: But the niches touch one another!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the corner arrangement from step 2.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The diagonal corner niche would overlap with the niches on the two neighboring walls, so the plan cannot physically work.

steps.title: רב אשי: dig them lower
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי answers that the corner niches are dug deeper, lower down in the wall.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: It is where he digs deeper.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי defends the corner plan. He says the diagonal niches are dug at a lower level, so they pass underneath the others.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The overlap problem only exists if all the niches are at the same height. If the diagonal niche is lower, it goes under the neighboring niches instead of hitting them. Now the corner plan works.

keyTerms.meaning: Where he digs deeper, meaning lower down in the wall
An אמורא who often gives the closing answer in a סוגיא

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said: It is where he digs deeper.
phrases.notes: He means the corner niche is dug lower in the wall, so it slips under the niches next to it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the overlap challenge of step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Clarifies how the case is built (different height)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: All niches are at the same level, so they would collide.
steps.terutzMaskana: The corner niches are dug lower, so there is no collision.

steps.title: Proof from רבי שמעון's four caves
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי shows that digging lower must be allowed, because otherwise רבי שמעון's four-cave layout could never be built.
steps.simpleTranslation: For if you do not say so, how would he make the four caves of רבי שמעון? The niches would touch one another!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי supports his answer with a proof. In the משנה, רבי שמעון describes four caves around one courtyard, and that layout has the same overlap problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With four caves sitting next to each other around a courtyard, the niches of one cave would run into the niches of the next cave. Since רבי שמעון clearly thought this layout could be built, there must be a solution. The only solution is digging some niches lower.

keyTerms.meaning: For if you do not say so: introduces a proof by showing the other option fails
Four caves around one courtyard, in רבי שמעון's layout
How?

phrases.english: For if you do not say so,
the four caves according to Rabbi Shimon:
phrases.notes: This refers to רבי שמעון in our משנה, who describes four caves on the four sides of a courtyard.

phrases.english: how does he make them?
The niches would touch one another!

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאִי לָא תֵּימָא הָכִי, אַרְבַּע מְעָרוֹת לְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב אשי's answer in step 4.
steps.raayaObject: That digging niches at a lower level is an accepted way to avoid overlap.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי שמעון's layout of four caves around a courtyard in the משנה.

steps.title: So here too, he digs deeper
steps.stepSummary: Just as רבי שמעון's caves must work by digging lower, רבי יוחנן's corner niches work the same way.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it must be where he digs deeper. Here too, it is where he digs deeper.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי closes his proof. רבי שמעון's caves only work if some niches are dug lower, so the corner niches here work the same way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof shows that digging lower is a normal, accepted way to build. רב אשי applies it to רבי יוחנן's corner plan. The overlap challenge from step 3 is now fully answered.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather: introduces the only workable option
Here too: applies the same idea to our case

steps.whatToRemember: The two niches opposite the entrance are dug diagonally in the back corners, as רבי יוחנן says. They do not overlap the other niches because they are dug lower, as רב אשי says. This is proven from רבי שמעון's four caves.

phrases.english: Rather, it is where he digs deeper;
here too, it is where he digs deeper.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion of the proof in step 5 and applies it to step 4.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Digging niches at a lower level solves the overlap, so רבי יוחנן's corner arrangement works.

steps.title: Angling the niches like a palm branch
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע offers another way to make רבי שמעון's four caves work: angle the niches outward like the leaves of a palm branch.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא son of רב יהושע said: רבי שמעון's four caves can work if you make the niches like a palm branch.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע gives another way to build רבי שמעון's four caves without digging lower: angle the niches outward like leaves on a palm branch, so they never meet. If he is right, רב אשי's proof from those caves would no longer hold.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אשי solved the overlap by changing the depth of the niches. רב הונא tries to solve it by changing their direction. If every niche slants away from the cave, the niches of neighboring caves should spread apart instead of colliding.

keyTerms.meaning: A palm branch, with leaves spreading out from the middle stem
Caves (burial chambers)
That one makes them

phrases.aramaic: רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אָמַר:
phrases.english: Rav Huna, son of Rav Yehoshua, said:
The four caves according to Rabbi Shimon
work where one makes them like a palm branch.
phrases.notes: Picture the niches slanting out from the cave the way palm leaves slant out from the stem.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains רבי שמעון's four caves without digging lower. If this were right, it would undercut רב אשי's proof in step 5, because that proof claimed digging lower was the only way the four caves could work. Step 8 rejects this explanation.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Niches of neighboring caves must collide unless they are dug at a different depth.
steps.terutzMaskana: Slanting the niches diagonally, like palm leaves, could keep them apart at the same depth.

steps.title: The geometry shows the palm-branch idea is a mistake
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא calculates that the diagonal space is only about 11⅕ אמות, which is too small for eight niches, so רב הונא's suggestion cannot work.
steps.simpleTranslation: This statement of רב הונא is a mistake. Every אמה of a square is 1⅖ אמות on its diagonal. So what does that come to? 11⅕. How many niches are there? Eight. How can eight fit into 11⅕? So רב הונא's statement is a mistake.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא does the math and shows there is not enough room along the diagonal to fit all the slanted niches.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The diagonal of a square is about 1⅖ times its side, so an 8-אמה side gives a diagonal of 11⅕ אמות. Eight niches have to fit along that line. Each niche needs width, and there must be solid rock between them. Eight cannot fit into 11⅕, so the palm-branch layout fails.

keyTerms.meaning: A mistake, an error
After all, since (introduces an obvious fact used as a proof)
A square
The diagonal
A fifth
Burial niches

steps.confusionAlert: Don't get lost in the numbers. The whole point is simple: the diagonal line is too short to hold eight niches with rock walls between them.

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא דְּרַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ – בְּרוּתָא הִיא.
phrases.english: And this statement of Rav Huna, son of Rav Yehoshua, is a mistake.
For after all, every cubit of a square
is a cubit and two-fifths on the diagonal;
how much does that come to for them?
phrases.notes: Each cave is 8 cubits long, so we are measuring the diagonal of an 8-by-8 square.

phrases.english: Eleven and one-fifth.
How many niches are there? Eight.
Eight in eleven and one-fifth,
how can you possibly find room for it?

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא הָא דְּרַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ – בְּרוּתָא הִיא.
phrases.english: Rather, this statement of Rav Huna, son of Rav Yehoshua, is a mistake.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא דְּרַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בְּרוּתָא הִיא
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Completely rejects רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע's palm-branch layout.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The diagonal (11⅕ אמות) is too short to hold eight niches with rock between them.

steps.title: The corner niches were small ones for stillborn babies
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives another answer to the corner-overlap problem: like רב שישא בריה דרב אידי said elsewhere, the corner niches were tiny ones for נפלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or if you want, say like רב שישא son of רב אידי said: with נפלים. Here too, with נפלים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the original problem of the corner niches running into their neighbors and offers a different answer from רב אשי's.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A נפל (a baby born dead or unable to live) needs only a very small burial niche. If the corner niches were made for נפלים, they are short and don't reach far enough to hit the neighboring niches. So there is no overlap, and there's no need to dig lower.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you wish, say (introduces another possible answer)
Stillborn babies, or babies who cannot survive (נפלים)
Here too

steps.whatToRemember: The overlap of the corner niches has two answers: רב אשי says they were dug lower, and the second answer says they were small niches for נפלים. The palm-branch idea was rejected.

phrases.english: And if you wish, say

phrases.aramaic: כִּדְאָמַר רַב שִׁישָׁא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִידִי:
phrases.english: as Rav Sheisha, son of Rav Idi, said:
It is for stillborn babies; here too, it is for stillborn babies.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי בָּעֵית אֵימָא כִּדְאָמַר רַב שִׁישָׁא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִידִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After rejecting the palm-branch idea, gives a second answer to the corner-overlap problem, alongside רב אשי's.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Corner niches are full-size and would run into neighboring niches.
steps.terutzMaskana: The corner niches were small ones for נפלים, so they don't reach the neighbors.

steps.title: A new משנה: finding one or two buried bodies
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens a new discussion by quoting a משנה in נזיר: someone who finds one or two bodies buried in the normal way removes them along with the earth around them.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in a משנה there: One who finds a dead body lying in the normal way removes it and the earth around it. If he finds two, he removes them and the earth around them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is starting a new topic. It quotes a משנה from נזיר to set up a discussion that relates to burial layouts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the base text for what comes next. The rule is that one or two bodies found buried normally may be moved, together with the earth that surrounds them. The גמרא will build on this משנה in the coming lines.

keyTerms.meaning: We learned in a משנה elsewhere
Lying in its normal way (buried the usual Jewish way)
The earth around it that it 'holds'

phrases.english: We learned in a mishna there:
One who finds a corpse lying in its usual manner
removes it and its surrounding earth.
If he finds two, he removes them and their surrounding earth.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the cave-niche discussion and opens a new topic with a quoted משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One or two bodies found buried in the normal way may be removed together with their surrounding earth.
